_comment: Mission objectives (spec: Mission objectives). A Mars flight picks one; its targets carry the share below of the science when the craft packs one of its instruments, so different designs win different objectives. Every value is a game rule: the instrument pairings follow what real Mars orbiters did, but the weights are the game's, not NASA's.

share.source: Game rule (Mission objectives): the objective's targets carry 60% of the science when a matching instrument is packed; the rest share 40% pro rata to their weights

metFraction.source: Game rule (Mission objectives): the objective is met when at least half of its targets' weight came home with a matching instrument

why.value: MAVEN dipped into the upper air with instruments that sniff and count its gases.
why.source: Game rule (Mission objectives): pairing after MAVEN, whose deep dips sampled the upper atmosphere

why.value: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter mapped the ground with a camera and looked under it with radar.
why.source: Game rule (Mission objectives): pairing after MRO's HiRISE camera and SHARAD radar

why.value: A spectrometer splits the light of Phobos and Deimos to find what they are made of.
why.source: Game rule (Mission objectives): pairing after orbiter spectrometers that observed Mars' moons (to verify which observations to cite)
